claims.text: Cold rolling followed by optimized annealing can refine the grain structure of MnNiSi-based magnetic-refrigeration materials.
The proposed thermomechanical treatment can increase the strength of MnNiSi-based materials.
The proposed thermomechanical treatment can improve the ductility of MnNiSi-based materials.
The large magnetocaloric effect can be largely preserved after microstructural refinement.
Conventionally cast MnNiSi-based material has a coarse-grained microstructure.
Conventionally cast MnNiSi-based material combines a large magnetic entropy change with poor mechanical properties or brittleness.
Cold rolling introduces plastic deformation and grain fragmentation in the target MnNiSi-based material.
Tailored annealing can relieve excessive strain without inducing detrimental phase changes.
Moderate room-temperature rolling followed by optimized annealing promotes grain refinement and defect healing while retaining the magnetic phase.
The treatment forms or preserves coherent interfaces.
Grain refinement and coherent interfaces improve load transfer and ductility through a Hall–Petch-type effect.
Increased grain-boundary area impedes dislocation motion and thereby enhances mechanical strength.
Grain refinement does not significantly modify the intrinsic magnetic exchange interactions responsible for the magnetocaloric effect.
Annealing can restore magnetic homogeneity and minimize defect-induced broadening of the magnetic transition.
Relative to the as-cast baseline, processed samples will have higher tensile strength and ductility without a significant decrease in maximum magnetic entropy change.
Excessive deformation or annealing may cause unwanted phase changes or chemical segregation that degrades magnetocaloric properties.
The large entropy change is dependent on preservation of a magnetostructural transition.
The hypothesis is falsified if mechanical performance fails to improve by more than 20% or if maximum magnetic entropy change decreases by more than approximately 10%.
